newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Wheat Pool aims to double hog output.
newsitem.headline: Sask Wheat Pool aims to double hog output.

text.p: Saskatchewan Wheat Pool said on Friday its acquisition of 1.4 million shares of Onex Corp's Fletcher's Fine Foods Ltd had the aim of at least doubling hog output in Saskatchewan.

"There are just over a million hogs produced annually in Saskatchewan and our objective is to increase that by two million hogs within the next four or five years," SWP chief executive Don Loewen said after the Fletcher's deal was announced.
Hog output in the western Canadian province has been static at 1.0 million in the past decade.
The Saskatchewan government is studying a farm-based request to end marketer Saskatchewan Pork International's monopoly after Manitoba and Alberta ended their monopolies in 1996.

Capacity at Fletcher's hog plant in Red Deer, Alberta, was expanded late last year to kill 8,000 hogs a day on two shifts. Another expansion was planned for the spring to kill 8,000 hogs a day on one shift, Fletcher's chief executive Fred Knoedler said.
SWP now owns 29 percent of Fletcher's. Between 40 and 50 percent of carcasses would be exported to the Pacific Rim and the United States.
"There are no plans at the present time to build a plant (in Saskatchewan). However, don't rule that out for the future," Knoedler added.
Western Canada's hog sector has been in flux since Canada scrapped its 98-year-old, C$56 million rail freight subsidy in August 1995, in compliance with a World Trade Organization deal.
The end of the subsidy means it costs more to ship grain to export points from the eastern Prairies than from anywhere else.
Farmers seeded more acreage of lower priced feed grains in the eastern Prairies last spring and many packers expanded there in anticipation of an increase in hog output.
SWP's acquisition of the Fletcher's Fine Foods shares at C$13.57 a share was the latest such development.
"We will always look at opportunities in the future but at this point in time we have no intention of buying more shares," Loewen said.
Since Fletcher's expanded late last year it has jousted with Canada's largest food processor, Maple Leaf Foods, for market share.
The subsequent rise in prices to farmers were drawing hogs from Saskatchewan and Manitoba, analysts said.
Manitoba Pool Elevators, another grain handling cooperative, has expressed interest in diversifying into the hog sector.
MPE and another cooperative, Alberta Wheat Pool, surprised the grain industry on Thursday when they raised their stake in United Grain Growers Ltd to 13 percent.
Some industry observers speculated SWP might now purchase UGG shares.
"We're an interested bystander in that situation but we're just watching and waiting," SWP's Loewen said.
